title: Exact operator bounds on Leggett-Garg violations
authors: Rathindra Nath Das, Arnab Kundu, Nemai Chandra Sarkar
abstract: Leggett-Garg (LG) inequalities test whether correlations measured at different times admit a positive joint probability distribution over histories. A violation requires negative values in any joint quasiprobability distribution reproducing those correlations, but such distributions can have negative values even without a violation. Spacetime density kernels extend the density-matrix description to multiple times and are used to study timelike entanglement. We establish a universal bound that relates LG violations to their negative eigenvalue weight. For LG tests involving any number of measurements, we determine the least compatible kernel negativity through an exact relation valid for any system dimension, initial state, dynamics, or measurement rule. This minimum is nonzero if and only if at least one LG inequality is violated. Three-time Lüders LG tests certify at most one eighth of negativity, whereas measurements resolving individual spin levels can approach one half. Including additional incompatible qubit observables gives a further exact minimum that can exceed the LG-only ceiling without increasing the LG violation.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes an exact, universal bound connecting violations of Leggett-Garg inequalities to the negativity of a constructed spacetime density kernel. By analyzing how correlations measured at multiple times constrain the quantum state, the authors provide a powerful diagnostic tool to quantify non-classical temporal correlations in quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental problem of testing Leggett-Garg (LG) inequalities, which determine if correlations measured at different times admit a positive joint probability distribution over histories.
main_result: The authors establish an exact, universal bound relating LG violations to the least compatible kernel negativity, showing that this minimum negativity is zero if and only if all LG inequalities are satisfied.
method: The methodology involves extending density matrices to 'spacetime density kernels' and deriving bounds on the negativity of these kernels based on measured pair correlations and additional observables.
model_or_system: The study analyzes quantum systems undergoing measurements at multiple time points, using the framework of spacetime density kernels to describe temporal correlations.
key_observables: Leggett-Garg (LG) violation, kernel negativity ($N$), pair correlations ($C_{ij}$), and the minimum compatible kernel negativity ($N_{\min}$).
important_parameters: The number of measurement times ($n$), the specific observables measured (e.g., $\sigma_z$ vs. $\sigma_x$), and the initial state/dynamics.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing compatible kernels that reproduce measured correlations, and it distinguishes between the minimum negativity required by a set of averages and the negativity of the full kernel.
figures_summary: Figures compare the minimum negativity ($N_{\min}$) revealed by different LG inequalities (e.g., $K_1, K_4, K_2, K_3$) for qubit measurements, contrasting results from Lüders protocols versus fully resolved measurements.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the LG test using pair correlations, then deriving the universal bound using spacetime kernels, and finally extending the analysis to include additional, incompatible observables to find tighter bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, quantitative bounds on non-classical temporal correlations, which is crucial for understanding quantum memory, quantum process tomography, and the limits of local realism in time.
